holidays.name: National Book Lovers Day
holidays.description: A day for bookworms to curl up with a favorite novel, ignore all social obligations, and proudly judge books by their covers (just this once).
holidays.origin: Started as an unofficial observance in the United States, popularized through social media and grassroots reading communities, encouraging people to put down their phones and pick up a good book.
holidays.funFact: The Japanese have a word, 'tsundoku', for buying books and letting them pile up unread, which describes many Book Lovers Day celebrants perfectly.

holidays.name: National Rice Pudding Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the creamy, comforting dessert made by simmering rice in sweetened milk, often spiced with cinnamon, nutmeg, or vanilla and sprinkled with raisins.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food holiday observed in the United States, honoring a dessert that has roots in cuisines worldwide, from Indian kheer to Scandinavian risalamande.
holidays.funFact: In Denmark, a Christmas rice pudding hides a single whole almond, and whoever finds it wins a prize, sometimes leading to people pretending not to have found it to keep the game going.

holidays.name: International Day of the World's Indigenous Peoples
holidays.description: A day to recognize and celebrate the cultures, languages, and contributions of Indigenous peoples around the globe while raising awareness of the challenges they face.
holidays.origin: Established by the United Nations General Assembly in December 1994, with the first observance in 1995, to mark the date of the first meeting of the UN Working Group on Indigenous Populations in 1982.
holidays.funFact: Indigenous peoples make up roughly 6% of the global population but are stewards of lands that hold a huge share of the world's remaining biodiversity, and they speak the majority of the world's roughly 7,000 languages.

holidays.name: Rice Pudding's Salty Cousin: National Hand Fan Day
holidays.description: A day to wave a hand fan dramatically in the dog days of summer, fluttering like a Victorian socialite or a Spanish flamenco dancer.
holidays.origin: An informal summer observance tied to the heat of early August, celebrating one of humanity's oldest cooling devices, which predates air conditioning by thousands of years.
holidays.funFact: In ancient Egypt, fan-bearer was a prestigious royal job, and Tutankhamun's tomb contained ceremonial fans made with ostrich feathers.

holidays.name: Nagasaki Peace Day
holidays.description: A solemn day of remembrance in Nagasaki, Japan, where people observe a moment of silence at 11:02 a.m., release doves, and call for a world free of nuclear weapons.
holidays.origin: It marks the anniversary of the 1945 atomic bombing of Nagasaki, with annual ceremonies held in Nagasaki Peace Park since the city began its peace declaration tradition after the war.
holidays.funFact: The Peace Statue in Nagasaki Peace Park has a raised right hand pointing to the threat of nuclear weapons and an outstretched left hand symbolizing eternal peace.
